name: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
problem: Standard attention is memory-bound: it materialises the full N x N attention matrix in HBM, so the cost of self-attention is dominated by HBM reads/writes rather than by FLOPs, and long sequences OOM.
mechanism: An IO-aware exact attention algorithm that never writes the N x N matrix to HBM. Tiles the computation into blocks that fit in SRAM, within each thread block loops over key/value blocks in SRAM-resident order, and accumulates the running softmax rescaling (m, l) and output accumulator on-chip in registers. Backward recomputes S = Q K^T instead of storing it. Exact - no approximation, no sparsity.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract), all vs the authors' own optimized baselines: 4-6x wall-clock speedup on BERT-large at seq length 512 vs the MLPerf 1.1 training speed record; 3x on GPT-2 at seq length 1K; 2.4x on Long Range Arena at seq lengths 1K-4K. Also first Transformers above chance on Path-X (16K, 61.4% acc) and Path-256 (64K, 63.1% acc).
